question.text: In Options on Goods, the tick size may be:

answer.text: Lower than that of the underlying commodity futures because it applies to option premium only
Always the same as the underlying futures
Always higher than futures tick size
Fixed at Re 1 for all commodity options

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, the tick size of Options on Goods may be lower than that of the underlying commodity futures because the tick applies to the option premium rather than to the full commodity price. The Trap: It is not always the same as futures, not always higher, and not fixed at Re 1 across all commodity options. Note: The tick size relates to how the option premium quotes move, not to the price of the underlying goods.
